findings.title: rustup toolchain install self-updates rustup in the CI, undoing the pin of rustup-init
findings.cause: the step "Rust, as rust-toolchain.toml pins it" downloads rustup-init 1.29.3 and checks it against a SHA-256 fixed in the workflow, then runs `rustup toolchain install` with rustup's default auto-self-update, `enable`; that command updates rustup itself to the newest release on static.rust-lang.org's update root, checked only against the `.sha256` the same server serves beside it. This machine showed it on 2026-11-06: `rustup toolchain install` updated rustup 1.29.0 to 1.29.3 (docs/toolchain.md's record). The pinned 1.29.3 is the newest today, so no run has updated yet; the first run after rustup's next release does
findings.consequence: whoever writes rustup's update root at static.rust-lang.org, content the CI fetches (security.md §1, last row), gets an unpinned rustup run in the build job that compiles the published binary, past the control of release.md §3 that names rustup-init pinned by its SHA-256; the same origin already serves the toolchain's manifest, which pins 1.99.1 by name alone, so the attacker set does not widen: the pin is weakened, no further damage shown. A new rustup release also changes the build's tool between two runs of the same tag, the reproducibility release.md §3 records
findings.fix: `rustup toolchain install --no-self-update` (the flag rustup 1.29.3 offers for that command), or `rustup set auto-self-update disable` right after rustup-init
findings.test: none: a workflow step; the proof is the step run in the pinned image, its log showing no "self-update" line and `rustup --version` printing 1.29.3 after the install, with actionlint on the workflow
findings.evidence: read: release.yml:51-54 runs rustup-init then `rustup toolchain install` with no self-update option; `rustup toolchain install --help` (rustup 1.29.3, this machine) prints "--no-self-update  Don't perform self update when running the `rustup toolchain install` command"; docs/toolchain.md:166-169 records the self-update from 1.29.0 to 1.29.3 at that command
findings.note: verified, its effect corrected: the self-update is real and runs the newest rustup-init with no checksum (the verifier, a fake update root on loopback), but rustup 1.29.3 skips it while CI is set; the run by hand's Rust step, its container given CI, prints no self-update line, so on GitHub it has no effect today. It holds where CI is unset, the podman reproductions of the steps, and the pin rests on a heuristic nothing in the repository states
findings.fixed_in: fix(ci): keep the pinned rustup from updating itself

findings.title: three crates of the toml family have a newer release within Cargo.toml's requirements
findings.cause: Cargo.lock holds serde_spanned 1.1.2, toml 1.2.0+spec-1.1.0 and toml_datetime 1.1.2+spec-1.1.0, while serde_spanned 1.1.3, toml 1.2.1+spec-1.1.0 and toml_datetime 1.1.3+spec-1.1.0, all released on 2026-11-06, satisfy the requirement toml = "1.1.8" and its transitive ones
findings.consequence: none today: no advisory names the locked versions; the lock lags a day behind the patch releases of the crate that parses the inventory and the configuration, and the next change takes them unreviewed
findings.fix: cargo update -p serde_spanned -p toml -p toml_datetime, then cargo deny check and cargo test under --locked
findings.test: none: a lock update within the requirements changes no behaviour a test could fail on before it; cargo deny check and the test suite run on the new lock are its proof
findings.evidence: read: dependencies.json, records serde_spanned (update 1.1.3), toml (update 1.2.1+spec-1.1.0), toml_datetime (update 1.1.3+spec-1.1.0), the three alone with a non-null update among 65 crates; Cargo.lock:401-402, 497-498, 512-513 hold the locked versions; Cargo.toml:21 toml = "1.1.8"
findings.fingerprint: dependencies | Cargo.lock + Cargo.toml | serde_spanned + toml + toml_datetime
findings.fixed_in: build(deps): update the toml crates within their requirements
